per_question.question: According to national decision-making policy E2, what factors should be considered when a development proposal is required to demonstrate whether an unmet need exists, including compliance with policy S5?
per_question.answer:
According to national decision-making policy E2, when a development proposal is required to demonstrate whether an unmet need exists, including compliance with policy S5, consideration should be given to whether market signals indicate an undersupply of specific types of land or premises (Draft_NPPF_December_2025, E2.2a). 
This includes taking into account the anticipated catchment area for the type of development proposed, the changing needs of different sectors, and the availability of existing land and buildings (Draft_NPPF_December_2025, E2.2a). 
Consideration should also be given to whether a development proposal’s specific locational requirements are met by existing allocations in the development plan (Draft_NPPF_December_2025, E2.2b).

per_question.question: According to policy GB6, under what circumstances can inappropriate development in the Green Belt be approved?
per_question.answer:
Inappropriate development in the Green Belt can be approved under policy GB6 when very special circumstances exist, and the potential harm to the Green Belt by reason of inappropriateness and any other harm resulting from the proposed development is clearly outweighed by other considerations (NPPF, GB6, paragraph 2). 
Substantial weight should be given to the harm to the Green Belt which would be caused, including harm to its openness (NPPF, GB6, paragraph 2).

per_question.question: According to the Green Belt assessment conducted in 2007 and the study in 2015, which parts of the Eastern Green site were identified as having potential for development and why?
per_question.answer:
The Green Belt assessment conducted in 2007 identified the southern part of the Eastern Green site as having potential for development (Coventry Planning Document, paragraph 136). The study conducted in 2015 also scored the area lower in recognition of the urbanising features towards the north east of the site around the golf course and hotel (Coventry Planning Document, paragraph 136). per_question.question: According to policy E1 in the National Planning Policy, what should development plans do to support business investment and employment?
per_question.answer:
To support business investment and employment, development plans should, at the most appropriate level, set out a clear economic vision and strategy, address potential barriers to investment, and allocate sites to implement the economic vision and strategy (NPPF, Policy E1). 
Development plans should take a positive, proactive and realistic approach to encouraging sustainable economic growth in both urban and rural areas, having regard to the Industrial Strategy and any relevant strategic and local strategies for economic development and regeneration (NPPF, Policy E1a). 
They should also take into account both local business needs and wider opportunities for economic growth, including priority places for investment in key sectors set out in the Industrial Strategy, and the location of Industrial Strategy Zones and AI Growth Zones (NPPF, Policy E1a). 
Additionally, development plans should seek to address potential barriers to investment, such as inadequate infrastructure, services or housing, or a poor environment (NPPF, Policy E1b).

per_question.question: According to the Supplementary Planning Document, what restrictions are placed on new vehicular access onto Kenilworth Road within the Conservation Area?
per_question.answer:
According to the Supplementary Planning Document, no new vehicular access is to be provided onto Kenilworth Road within the Conservation Area (Kenilworth Road control plan, 2.4). per_question.question: According to Annex B: Glossary in this planning document, what are the three main types of affordable housing defined?
per_question.answer:
The three main types of affordable housing defined in Annex B: Glossary are: Social Rent, Other affordable housing for rent, and housing that provides a subsidised route to home ownership (Draft_NPPF_December_2025, Annex B). 
Social Rent is defined as housing that meets all of the following conditions: the rent is set in accordance with the government’s rent policy for Social Rent, the landlord is a registered provider, and it includes provisions to remain at an affordable price for future eligible households, or for the subsidy to be recycled for alternative affordable housing provision (Draft_NPPF_December_2025, Annex B). 
Other affordable housing for rent meets all of the following conditions: the rent is set in accordance with the government’s rent policy for Affordable Rent, or is at least 20% below local market rents (Draft_NPPF_December_2025, Annex B).

per_question.question: According to the Coventry Planning Document, what are the key considerations for potential residential development on Parcel 15b (south of the railway line and west of Cromwell Lane)?
per_question.answer:
Parcel 15b, located south of the railway line and west of Cromwell Lane, is described as gently sloping open farmland with little tree cover and no recorded areas of ecological importance or major physical constraints (Coventry Planning Document, GREEN_BELT_REVIEW_Annex_2). 
The site has potential for residential development, with access from Cromwell Lane, subject to sensitive design considerations (Coventry Planning Document, GREEN_BELT_REVIEW_Annex_2). 
Key considerations for development include protecting the setting of the Grade II Listed farmhouse at Westwood Farm and boundary native woodland planting to protect the visual amenities of the Green Belt and enhance its ecological value (Coventry Planning Document, GREEN_BELT_REVIEW_Annex_2). 
The site's location adjacent to the railway station and close to the facilities of Tile Hill Village makes it a suitable location for sustainable residential development (Coventry Planning Document, GREEN_BELT_REVIEW_Annex_2).

per_question.question: According to policy HO4, what requirements must the development plan meet when identifying locations for large scale residential and mixed-use development?
per_question.answer:
According to policy HO4, the development plan should identify suitable locations for large scale development, such as new settlements, new urban quarters or significant extensions to existing settlements (NPPF, HO4:1). 
These locations should be capable of being supported by the necessary infrastructure and facilities at appropriate points in the development’s delivery (NPPF, HO4:1a). 
They should also support a sustainable community, with sufficient access to services and employment opportunities within the development itself, or in larger towns to which there is good access by sustainable transport modes (NPPF, HO4:1b). 
Additionally, they should address strategic environmental opportunities and safeguards, including those set out in Local Nature Recovery Strategies (NPPF, HO4:1c). 
Local plans should identify specific sites, infrastructure and other site-specific requirements for large-scale development (NPPF, HO4:2). 
This includes setting clear expectations for the quality of places to be created, making a realistic assessment of the likely rates of delivery, and supporting delivery by setting expectations for an appropriate mix of tenures (NPPF, HO4:2a-c).

per_question.answer:
The baseline for local housing need is calculated as 0.8% of the existing housing stock for the area (NPPF, paragraph 3). The existing housing stock is determined using the Dwelling Stock Estimates data published annually (NPPF, paragraph 3).

per_question.question: According to the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015, what does an Article 4 direction do?
per_question.answer:
An Article 4 direction withdraws permitted development rights granted by the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) (England) Order 2015 (NPPF, paragraph as cited in glossary). 
A direction under Article 4(2) of the General Development Order brings under the control of the local planning authority any specified developments normally permitted under the Town and Country Planning (General Permitted Development) Order 2015 (Coventry Local Plan Review Evidence Base, LP Appendices 2023, definition of Article 4 Direction). 
The use of Article 4 directions to remove permitted development rights should be limited to situations where it is necessary to protect local amenity or the wellbeing of the area (Draft NPPF December 2025, DM10). 
An Article 4 Direction came into effect on 30th September 2023, removing HMO permitted development rights in certain wards of Coventry (Authority Monitoring Report 2023/24, paragraph 3.15).

per_question.question: According to the Coventry Planning Document, what is the definition of 'Major Development' and which Act should be referenced for its definition unless otherwise stated?
per_question.answer:
The definition of 'Major Development' is outlined in the Coventry Local Plan as: a) The use of land for mineral working deposits; b) Waste development; c) All forms of residential development where: (i) The number of homes to be provided is 150 or more; or (ii) The site area is 5 hectares or more and it is not known whether the development falls within sub-paragraph (c)(i); d) All forms of urban development (not involving housing) where: (i) The area of development exceeds 1 hectare; or (ii) In the case of industrial estate development exceeds 5 hectares (Health Impact Assessment SPD, Section 3). 
Unless otherwise stated, the definition should be referenced from the Town and Country Planning (Development Management Procedure) Order 2015 (DMPO) as amended, which is implied to be the relevant Act for its definition (Statement of Community Involvement, Paragraph 3.3).

per_question.question: According to policy HO12, what criteria must development proposals for traveller sites meet regarding site design and integration with the community?
per_question.answer:
According to policy HO12, development proposals for traveller sites must be located and designed so that they provide a settled base that limits the need for long-distance travelling and potential environmental damage caused by unauthorised encampment (Draft_NPPF_December_2025, HO12.1a). 
They must enable access to education, welfare, and health services, including ensuring that children can attend school on a regular basis (Draft_NPPF_December_2025, HO12.1b). 
Proposals must promote opportunities for healthy lifestyles, such as by providing adequate landscaping and play areas for children, and minimising adverse impacts from local environmental factors on the health and wellbeing of travellers (Draft_NPPF_December_2025, HO12.1c). 
They must not enclose the site such that the site and its occupants appear to be isolated from the rest of the community (Draft_NPPF_December_2025, HO12.1d).

per_question.question: According to policy DM1 in the National Planning Policy, what are the requirements for proposals for major development before submitting a planning application?
per_question.answer:
According to policy DM1 in the National Planning Policy, proposals for major development should be informed by early engagement with neighbours and the local community, as well as with the local planning authority, statutory consultees and other relevant bodies where appropriate, to identify and seek to resolve key planning matters prior to the submission of a planning application (National Planning Policy, DM1.1a). 
Proposals for major development should also be accompanied by a concise planning statement setting out how the proposals are consistent with relevant development plan and national decision-making policies, the outcome of pre-application engagement and the extent to which the proposals have changed in response to this engagement, and the proposed use of any planning obligations to make the proposals acceptable in planning terms (National Planning Policy, DM1.1b).

per_question.question: Which policies in the Coventry City Centre Area Action Plan (CC1, CC8, CC9, CC11) are identified as requiring a fresh SA/SEA assessment due to substantive changes, according to the March 2017 Sustainability Appraisal/Strategic Environmental Assessment Addendum Report?
per_question.answer:
Policies CC1, CC8, CC9, and CC11 in the Coventry City Centre Area Action Plan are identified as requiring a fresh SA/SEA assessment due to substantive changes (MOD13_SASEA___CCAAP_Proposed_Modifications_2017, Page 34 of 48; MOD13_SASEA___CCAAP_Proposed_Modifications_2017, Page 29-30 of 48 is not relevant but  MOD13_SASEA___CCAAP_Proposed_Modifications_2017, Page 34 of 48 and others are) (Coventry City Centre Area Action Plan – Proposed Modifications, March 2017 Sustainability Appraisal/Strategic Environmental Assessment Addendum Report, Policy CC1, CC8, CC9, CC11). 
Specifically, CC1 has a number of changes proposed including a more inclusive reference to integrated University development, public transport system integration and supporting green and blue infrastructure (MOD13_SASEA___CCAAP_Proposed_Modifications_2017, Page 29 of 48 is not the exact reference, the correct one is) (MOD13_SASEA___CCAAP_Proposed_Modifications_2017, Policy Summary of Changes). 
CC8 has a number of small adjustments proposed in the supporting text to reflect the updated flood risk and drainage policies in the draft Local Plan (MOD13_SASEA___CCAAP_Proposed_Modifications_2017, Policy CC8). 
CC9 also has a number of small adjustments proposed in the supporting text to reflect the updated flood risk and drainage policies in the draft Local Plan (MOD13_SASEA___CCAAP_Proposed_Modifications_2017, Policy CC9). 
CC11 has continued engagement with TfWM leading to a small number of adjustments to strengthen links to sub-regional and regional public transport and cycle networks (MOD13_SASEA___CCAAP_Proposed_Modifications_2017, Policy CC11). 
Due to the substantive changes to these policies, it is considered that they represent a significant change to the findings of the SA/SEA report, which would require a fresh SA/SEA assessment (MOD13_SASEA___CCAAP_Proposed_Modifications_2017, Policy CC1, CC8, CC9, CC11).

per_question.question: According to the provided chunk, which types of infrastructure are classified as 'Essential Infrastructure' in flood risk areas?
per_question.answer:
The types of infrastructure classified as 'Essential Infrastructure' in flood risk areas are: Essential transport infrastructure (including mass evacuation routes) which has to cross the area at risk (Draft_NPPF_December_2025, Table 2); Essential utility infrastructure which has to be located in a flood risk area for operational reasons, including infrastructure for electricity supply including generation, storage and distribution systems; and water treatment works that need to remain operational in times of flood (Draft_NPPF_December_2025, Table 2); Wind turbines (Draft_NPPF_December_2025, Table 2); Solar farms (Draft_NPPF_December_2025, Table 2); Hydrogen production facilities (Draft_NPPF_December_2025, Table 2); Carbon Capture, distribution and storage facilities (Draft_NPPF_December_2025, Table 2); Data Centres (Draft_NPPF_December_2025, Table 2); Electric vehicle charging stations (Draft_NPPF_December_2025, Table 2).

per_question.question: According to the Coventry Green Belt Review, 2007, what recommendation is made regarding the Coundon Court School buildings and their Green Belt status?
per_question.answer:
According to the Coventry Green Belt Review, 2007, it is recommended that the Coundon Court School buildings are taken out of the Green Belt to enable redevelopment for sustainable long-term educational needs, but only to the extent necessary (Coventry Green Belt Review, 2007, Section 4.18). The built area of the school should be released from the Green Belt, and the boundary should be carefully drawn to ensure that the tree cover is maintained in perpetuity (Coventry Green Belt Review, 2007, Section 5.7.7). It is also recommended that additional tree planting takes place to reinforce what is there already and that tree preservation orders are placed on the trees in this area (Coventry Green Belt Review, 2007, Section 5.7.7).

With the growth of the city and the BSF programme there are clear exceptional needs to adjust Green Belt boundaries to meet long-term strategic requirements. Therefore, it is recommended that the Coundon Court School buildings are taken out of the Green Belt to enable redevelopment for sustainable long term educational needs, but only to the extent necessary. This should not include the mature trees which are critical in shielding the existing (and potential) buildings from the broader views across the wedge. per_question.question: What substantive change to Policy HE3 in the Coventry Local Plan – Proposed Modifications, March 2017 requires a fresh SA/SEA assessment?
per_question.answer:
The substantive change to Policy HE3 in the Coventry Local Plan – Proposed Modifications, March 2017 that requires a fresh SA/SEA assessment is that the policy has been developed in partnership with Bluecoats School and the Charterhouse Trust and clarifies the position around how the heritage park will be delivered and how the future expansion of the school can be supported (MOD14_SASEA_Final_Report___Local_Plan_Proposed_Modfications_2017, Policy HE3). It also brings into the policy the specific requirement for a comprehensive Masterplan developed in partnership with both parties alongside the city council and local community (MOD14_SASEA_Final_Report___Local_Plan_Proposed_Modfications_2017, Policy HE3). Due to these substantive changes to the policy, it is considered that this represents a significant change to the findings of the SA/SEA report, which would require a fresh SA/SEA assessment (MOD14_SASEA_Final_Report___Local_Plan_Proposed_Modfications_2017, Policy HE3).

per_question.question: According to the City Centre Area Action Plan – Proposed Submission Sustainability Appraisal Report (January 2016), what are the main benefits of the 'Focused' option for new office development in Coventry city centre?
per_question.answer:
The main benefits of the 'Focused' option for new office development in Coventry city centre are that it would result in office development being located where it is most accessible by public transport and would promote rail travel as a principle form of transport for office workers (City Centre Area Action Plan – Proposed Submission Sustainability Appraisal Report, January 2016, Page 21 of 104). This option would also decrease the levels of air pollution in the city centre and decrease energy consumption through the greater use of renewables (City Centre Area Action Plan – Proposed Submission Sustainability Appraisal Report, January 2016, Page 21 of 104). Furthermore, it would reduce road congestion, which in turn would help to prevent Coventry being seen as an unattractive location for firms to locate (City Centre Area Action Plan – Proposed Submission Sustainability Appraisal Report, January 2016, Page 22 of 104). The 'Focused' option would also contribute to defining the City Centre as Coventry’s premium office-based employment hub, reducing car use and encouraging public transport (City Centre Area Action Plan – Proposed Submission Sustainability Appraisal Report, January 2016, Page 28 of 104).

per_question.question: According to policy DP1 in the National Planning Policy, what should development plans do to set out clear design expectations?
per_question.answer:
According to policy DP1 in the National Planning Policy, development plans should set out clear design expectations by: ensuring the vision for the plan reflects the desired design and placemaking outcomes (NPPF, DP1.1a); identifying where design guides, design codes and masterplans are necessary to deliver design and placemaking outcomes (NPPF, DP1.1b); setting out locally-specific design policies or standards which are necessary to add further detail to the principles in policy DP3 (NPPF, DP1.1c); and setting out in what circumstances design review and other design processes will be required (NPPF, DP1.1d).

per_question.question: According to policy F6, under what circumstances must the 'exception test' be satisfied for development proposals in flood zones 2, 3a, or 3b?
per_question.answer:
According to policy F6, the 'exception test' must be satisfied for development proposals in flood zones 2, 3a, or 3b in certain circumstances shown in Annex F, table 3, in addition to satisfying the sequential test in policy F5 where applicable (Draft_NPPF_December_2025, Policy F6). per_question.question: According to policy CC1 in the National Planning Policy, what proactive approaches should development plans take to mitigate and adapt to climate change?
per_question.answer:
According to policy CC1 in the National Planning Policy, development plans should take a proactive approach to mitigating climate change and supporting the transition to net zero (NPPF, Policy CC1). They should also take a proactive approach to adapting to climate change, taking into account the implications of extreme weather and long-term climate trends (NPPF, Policy CC1). This includes proposing development patterns through their spatial strategy and allocations which can help contribute to radical reductions in greenhouse gas emissions and avoid increased vulnerability and improve resilience to the effects of climate change (NPPF, Policy CC1, subsection 1a). Development plans should address any specific risks from climate change in their proposed allocations for development and necessary adaptations (NPPF, Policy CC1, subsection 1b). They should also identify opportunities for green infrastructure provision and nature-based solutions which can safeguard and improve carbon storage, support nature recovery and resilience (NPPF, Policy CC1, subsection 1d).

- NPPF: Draft_NPPF_December_2025.pdf — Policy CC1, subsection 1a, 1b, 1d

per_question.question: According to the Supplementary Planning Document (SPD) for Tall Buildings and the Three Spires View Management Framework in Coventry, what is a key consideration for any application for tall buildings in and around the city centre?
per_question.answer:
Retaining the views of the city's iconic three spires, and the spires' primacy in the city centre skyline, is a key consideration in any application for tall buildings in and around the city centre (Tall Buildings Design Guide and View Management Framework SPD, paragraph 1.4). 
The location of proposed tall buildings will be considered in relation to the views of the city's three spires (City Centre Area Action Plan, Policy CC7).

per_question.answer:

per_question.question: According to policy TR5, under what circumstances should development proposals for roadside facilities located outside settlements be permitted?
per_question.answer:
According to policy TR5, development proposals for roadside facilities located outside settlements should be permitted under the following circumstances: 
they should meet an evidenced need to improve the safety and welfare of road users, or to improve access to electric vehicle charging infrastructure or other alternative fuels, if new or significantly expanded facilities are being proposed (Draft_NPPF_December_2025, TR5.1a); 
or they should improve driver welfare and security, support changes in transport technology, or improve environmental impacts, where the proposal is to upgrade existing facilities without significant expansion (Draft_NPPF_December_2025, TR5.1b).

per_question.answer:
Option A was moved away from because it represents a non-viable or achievable alternative due to the viability of solely retail-led regeneration (City Centre Area Action Plan – Proposed Submission Sustainability Appraisal Report, January 2016, Page 25 of 104). 
Option B was identified as the most appropriate as it maintains an appropriate balance and platform from which to focus the city centre's retail core (City Centre Area Action Plan – Proposed Submission Sustainability Appraisal Report, January 2016, Page 25 of 104). 
Option B scored the least number of negatives and is considered the most sustainable, with Option B also attracting a higher number of double positives (City Centre Area Action Plan – Proposed Submission Sustainability Appraisal Report, January 2016, Page 54 of 104).

per_question.question: According to the draft Air Quality SPD for Coventry, what assessments are major developments required to undertake, and in what circumstances might smaller developments also require assessments?
per_question.answer:
Major developments are required to undertake full air quality assessments (Cabinet_Member_Report_air_quality_SPD_final_draft_10_Dec_2018, paragraph 1.5). Where appropriate, exposure assessments will also apply to smaller developments in accordance with the guidance (Cabinet_Member_Report_air_quality_SPD_final_draft_10_Dec_2018, paragraph 1.5). The draft Air Quality SPD sets out the methodology for identifying development proposals where an air quality assessment will be required, and the processes involved (Cabinet_Member_Report_air_quality_SPD_final_draft_10_Dec_2018, paragraph 1.6).

per_question.question: According to the Coventry Local Plan – Proposed Modifications, March 2017 Sustainability Appraisal/Strategic Environmental Assessment Addendum Report, how was the Sustainability Appraisal of the Local Plan Proposed Modifications carried out?
per_question.answer:
The Sustainability Appraisal of the Local Plan Proposed Modifications was carried out in two stages: Stage A, the production of a Scoping Report, and Stage B, the production of the Sustainability Appraisal Addendum Report, 2017 (MOD14_SASEA_Final_Report___Local_Plan_Proposed_Modfications_2017, paragraph 1.4). 
The first stage involved reviewing relevant plans, programmes, and strategies, collecting information to develop an understanding of the social, environmental, and economic health of the city, and identifying key sustainability issues (MOD14_SASEA_Final_Report___Local_Plan_Proposed_Modfications_2017, paragraph 1.5). 
The Sustainability Appraisal Framework was developed to assess the Local Plan in a systematic and logical way (MOD14_SASEA_Final_Report___Local_Plan_Proposed_Modfications_2017, paragraph 1.5). 
A range of options were put forward to address the key planning issues facing the city up to 2031 and were appraised against each of the Sustainability Objectives (MOD14_SASEA_Final_Report___Local_Plan_Proposed_Modfications_2017, paragraph 1.6). 
The effects of the Local Plan were predicted and evaluated in terms of their magnitude, geographical scale, and time period over which they will occur (MOD14_SASEA_Final_Report___Local_Plan_Proposed_Modfications_2017, paragraph 1.6). 
Mitigation measures were proposed to prevent, reduce, or offset significant effects or to maximise beneficial impacts (MOD14_SASEA_Final_Report___Local_Plan_Proposed_Modfications_2017, paragraph 1.6).

References:
- MOD14_SASEA_Final_Report___Local_Plan_Proposed_Modfications_2017: Coventry Local Plan – Proposed Modifications, March 2017 Sustainability Appraisal/Strategic Environmental Assessment Addendum Report — paragraphs 1.4, 1.5, 1.6
contexts: to promote sustainable development through the integration of economic, environmental and social considerations into the preparation of plans and proposals. A key function of the Sustainability Appraisal is to illustrate the positives and identify and allowable negatives when appraising alternative site and policy options, thus informing a transparent decision making process. Purpose and Structure of this SA Addendum Report 1.3 The purpose of this SA Addendum Report is to clearly set out the method and findings of further SA work carried out as a result of the proposed modifications to the Local Plan Examination. per_question.question: According to Policy GE1 Green Infrastructure in the Coventry Local Plan – Proposed Modifications, March 2017, what must new development proposals do regarding green infrastructure?
per_question.answer:
New development proposals should make provision for green infrastructure to ensure that such development is integrated into the landscape and contributes to improvements in connectivity and public access, biodiversity, landscape conservation, design, archaeology and recreation (Coventry Local Plan – Proposed Modifications, March 2017, Policy GE1). 
New development will be expected to maintain the quantity, quality and functionality of existing green infrastructure (Coventry Local Plan – Proposed Modifications, March 2017, Policy GE1). 
Where quantity is not retained, enhancement to quality is expected (Coventry Local Plan – Proposed Modifications, March 2017, Sustainability Appraisal/Strategic Environmental Assessment Addendum Report, Page 81 of 99). 
Where the opportunity arises, and in line with the city's most up-to-date Green Space Strategy, the Council will also expect new developments to enhance green infrastructure, and create and improve linkages between individual areas (Coventry Local Plan – Proposed Modifications, March 2017, Sustainability Appraisal/Strategic Environmental Assessment Addendum Report, Page 81 of 99).

per_question.question: According to the Supplementary Planning Document, what is the SPD's stance on the replication of traditional Ancient Arden design elements in new developments as stated on page 7?
per_question.answer:
The SPD's stance on the replication of traditional Ancient Arden design elements in new developments as stated on page 7 is that there is no fundamental expectation that these will be replicated verbatim across new developments (Appendix_2___Consultation_Statement___SUE_Design_Guidance, Page 7). However, these elements are intended to provide a helpful reference for how the more traditional elements of Ancient Arden design can be incorporated and interpreted within new development proposals (Appendix_2___Consultation_Statement___SUE_Design_Guidance, Page 7).

References:
- Appendix_2___Consultation_Statement___SUE_Design_Guidance: Supplementary Planning Document — Page 7
contexts: and proximity to the city itself. This should be covered. The guidance does set out the character of the area. Even if we accept that some of the immediate area and its character have been compromised it is no excuse in itself to justify a bog-standard form of development within the SUEs - especially when we are talking about a substantial level of development within an undulating and otherwise undeveloped landscape. As such, this design guidance is intended to be positive and reflect future development this draws on good examples within the local area. It is not intended to pick out existing properties that cannot be influenced by the guidance. The SPD is not reflective of an SUE of this size being delivered by major housebuilders. The statement on page 6 regarding the "very much traditional vernacular" is not an appropriate objective for a modern SUE especially in view of the examples. The guidance on page 7 is also too prescriptive and more suited to a Conservation Area. Page 6 says: "It is important to note that whilst this is very much a traditional vernacular it will not be used as a basis to preclude creative, well thought out and innovative designs. As previously highlighted, modern interpretation of these historic characteristics are welcomed and encouraged and will always be treated on their own merits." Page 7 then stats "There is no fundamental expectation that these will be replicated verbatim across new developments, however these are intended to provide a helpful reference for how the more traditional

elements of Ancient Arden design can be incorporated and interpreted within new development proposals." As such, we do not consider this too prescriptive - no change is proposed. The guidance fails to take account of what can be realistically delivered by housebuilders e.g. sash windows are not widely used in commercial housebuilding due to implications for building regulation related to fire ingress and escape routes. We respectfully disagree and are aware of numerous examples across the country where such options are incorporated into new build developments. The scale of these developments also offer a degree of scale to support such opportunities. These issues can also be considered further through the planning application stages. In terms of Building Regulations it is our understanding that any window at first floor level needs to facilitate a means of escape and incorporate an area of 0.33sq.m with at least one length of the windows being 450mm. It is our view that this can be managed through a wide range of window types meaning the guidance would be appropriate in terms of Building Regulations and fire safety. No changes are proposed to the guidance. There are other examples of features that are unlikely to be commercially viable at this scale including roof pitches at 40 degrees, tile verges, the specific mix of bricks, dormer windows with eaves below 2 stories and real chimney stacks. These features would be more suited to landmark buildings rather than general design. The guidance reflects this and would allow for such proposals. The guidance is not

be considered in the context of the SUE and on their own merits. The primary focus for non- development will be along the Hill fort view corridor, moving down into Hounds Hill and the Hall Brook corridor. This is outlined in the indicative masterplan. Examples provided on pages 7-12 are not relevant to a large scale development such as the SUE's and as such are not necessary to include. Comment noted, however these examples are not reflective of the exact developments we expect to see within the SUE, but instead establish good examples of the sort of materials and design principles that we would expect to see reflected in the new developments. This is set out in the draft SPD as a principle and has previously been communicated. This reflects the lack of larger scale developments within this character area. Many of the example are not local (e.g. pages 15-19) and are not relevant to the Arden Comment noted, unfortunately there are very limited examples of local developments within this area that are reflective of scale and context that the 2 SUEs will deliver. It’s for this reason that we have sought to bring together examples of small scale developments in the local area with good practice examples from wider afield to help show how the principle of local vernacular can be utilised and interpreted in larger scale developments. When discussing the historic character of the Arden there is little recognition that the area has already been compromised by recent developments e.g. Tamworth Road, power lines

a requirement for a slavish recreation of all Arden characteristics within every single property. The guidance invites modern creative approaches and interpretation to traditional characteristics. We would agree though that feature buildings or landmark buildings could be used in a more traditional way. In the housing design section the SPD states that a diverse approach to housing design is encouraged and that this will ensure there is a variety of character and texture across the developments as opposed to a homogenous swathe of development. If this is a key objective it is generally supported and should be clarified in earlier sections. Comment noted. In our view this is reflected throughout the document. There is no local/ Arden evidence to support linked dwellings. If used on all street types it will result in homogenous street scenes which conflicts with wider aims and objectives. There are examples of smaller scale linked dwellings and the courtyard example also lends itself towards this. We have used these by way of example to help highlight a good quality street scene. We would not expect them to be used continuously across the whole development but they are an option as part of the main street scenes and a way of helping incorporate on plot car parking. Linked dwellings can create difficulties in meeting parking requirements without relying on on-street parking which in turn can affect the street scene. This is not our experience in the schemes we have researched and not our intention for any examples here. It’s not our intention for

masterplan should be updated as different parcels of the scheme progress and become finalised. Comment noted, an additional sentence has been added into the introductory section to confirm this. I applaud the aim and substance of this document and look forward to seeing it again during any final consultation. Ensuring high quality and appropriate design which conforms to the philosophy of the Ancient Arden could make the delivery of new homes more tolerable for existing residents. We just need to make sure the standards are enforced. Comment noted and support for the guidance is welcomed. The adoption of the SPD will give it strong material weight in the determination of planning applications. This will help ensure the Council can ensure high quality design in accordance with the document. Support SPD and inclusion of natural landscape section with specific examples. Comment noted. SPD should require the 2 SUE areas to deliver a net gain in biodiversity in accordance with NPPF and Government's 25 year plan for the environment Comment noted - This will be supported through wider Local Plan policy (GE3) however an additional sentence has been added to Page 80 for clarification. Page 74 - boundary demarcation - we would recommend that permeable boundary features such as small gaps in walls and fences and gaps below gates are recommended in this section. This will help support the movement of wildlife and support their valuable habitats. Point noted, connectivity to support movement of wildlife is a key component of the overarching local plan policies and is reflected
per_question.ground_truth: The SPD states on page 7 that there is no fundamental expectation for traditional Ancient Arden design elements to be replicated verbatim in new developments; instead, these elements are intended as helpful references for incorporation and interpretation within proposals.
